lines.text: Could you guess how thirty Greek soldiers survived inside the Trojan Horse before Troy burned?
Built from dismantled ship timber, the belly wasn't just a hollow box. It held two narrow scaffolding tiers where soldiers sat shoulder-to-shoulder in complete silence.
At thirty-five degrees Celsius, body heat alone would cause suffocation in hours. The builders hid microscopic air vents disguised inside the nostrils, ears, and horse mane.
When night fell and Troy slept, Odysseus unlocked a spring-loaded trapdoor beneath the horse's belly, dropping hemp ropes to the cobblestones below.
Within minutes, the gates were thrown wide open. The city that resisted a ten-year siege fell in a single night... from the inside out.
